This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by the Hong Kong Observatory in degrees Celsius on 16 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the Hong Kong Observatory, specifically the "Absolute Daily Max (deg. C)" the specified date once information is finalized in the relevant "Daily Extract", available here: https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/cis/climat.htm

This market can not resolve until data for this date has been published.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures in Celsius to one decimal place (eg, 9.1°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is initially published for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Hong Kong Observatory readings on 16 August reached a daytime maximum of 33.2–33.6 °C under partly cloudy skies with scattered showers and light winds, consistent with model consensus for peak values near 33 °C. Following the 9 August record of 36.9 °C driven by Typhoon Dolphin’s warm-air advection, a return to typical summer monsoon flow with increased cloud cover and localized convection has suppressed further heating. Official HKO data and regional station reports confirm this moderation against August climatological averages of 31–32 °C, leaving limited scope for deviation unless subsidence strengthens unexpectedly before evening observations finalize the daily high.

**Trader consensus around 18–19°C for Cape Town’s August 18 maximum reflects typical mid-winter Mediterranean conditions, where the long-term average high sits near 17–18°C.** Recent forecasts from the South African Weather Service and global models indicate partly cloudy skies with light to moderate north-westerly winds, supporting modest daytime heating without strong frontal influences or significant cloud cover that would suppress temperatures.

The tight spread between the two leading outcomes stems from small but meaningful differences in ensemble guidance: subtle shifts in wind direction or speed can add or subtract 1°C of warming, while variable low-level moisture and timing of any weak Atlantic systems introduce model spread. Historical analogs for mid-August show maxima clustering between 16–20°C, with 18°C occurring most frequently under similar synoptic setups.

Resolution depends on the official maximum recorded at Cape Town’s primary observing stations, so traders are closely watching the next 24–48 hours of updated model runs and official briefings for any late adjustments in the forecast.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity is the dominant driver capping Manila's peak temperatures on August 18, with official PAGASA guidance showing a 31°C high but widespread cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and 60% rain probability suppressing solar insolation. Recent model runs and rainfall outlooks emphasize heavy monsoon flow across Luzon, consistent with typical wet-season patterns that historically keep daily maxima near 28–30°C rather than seasonal averages near 31°C. Traders' concentration on 28–29°C reflects this expectation of reduced insolation and evaporative cooling from precipitation, while lower-probability warmer outcomes would require clearer skies or delayed monsoon strengthening. Updated PAGASA briefings and ensemble forecasts over the next 48 hours remain the key variables that could shift resolution criteria.
